newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Stals hopeful of S.Africa rate cut, timing unclear.
newsitem.headline: Stals hopeful of S.Africa rate cut, timing unclear.

text.p: South African Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals on Thursday reiterated his belief that recent inflation and money supply data was encouraging and could pave the way for a rate cut before the end of the year.
But he told Reuters it was impossible to be precise as to when conditions would be right to cut the key Bank rate from its current 17 percent level.
"All we can say is that hopefully in the second half of this year the situation will get easier on the financial side of the economy and it will be possible to relax on the monetary policy," he said.
"But exactly when and by exactly how much is not possible to say."

On Monday, the central bank released data showing money supply growth slowed to a preliminary 12.79 percent rise in June from 15.32 percent in May and bank credit extension growth up 16.39 percent from 16.65 percent in June.

That was followed on Tuesday by data showing annual inflation at a nine-month low of 8.8 percent in June and Customs and Excise data showing South Africa's trade balance swelled to 4.15 billion rand in the same month from 1.75 billion rand in May.
